description_full: Santacruz Silver Mining Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the acquisition, exploration, development, production, and operation of mineral properties in Latin America. The company primarily explores for silver and zinc, as well as lead and copper deposits. It also holds a portfolio of mineral properties in Mexico and Bolivia. The company is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.
ceo_bio: Mr. Arturo  Prestamo Elizondo CPA | CEO & Executive Chairman | Compensation: $617,773 (FY2025)
financial_summary: Santacruz Silver Mining Ltd. is a small-cap basic materials business with a $635M market cap on $326M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +8.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 28% against a 10% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 14% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $48M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.87× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 30× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 6.9% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sector_headwinds.text: Weakness in commodity prices pressures materials companies
Commodity price volatility and cost-curve position — in a downturn only the lowest-cost producer has a business, and the rest carry the overhead.
Environmental remediation liability — tightening regulations on emissions, tailings, and water use create open-ended balance-sheet risk that grows with each legislative cycle.
Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

sect: Its 25% operating margin runs 16pp above the Basic Materials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.95x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 221 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 53% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 19% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 61% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 92% and a beta of 1.05, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 3.31 vs 5y 1.23), so read it loosely.
About $3.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 58% in the 2020 crash and 55% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades only 2% below its DCF fair value of $6.98, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 24%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $5.32 to $9.45 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: EV/EBITDA 4.4 vs 8.3 and P/FCF 13.1 vs 22.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 7.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 13.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The Street target $15.00 on average, 120% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 6.3% annual cash-flow growth.
prof: ROIC of 28% clears the cost of capital of 9.5% by 18pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.25).
It runs a 14% gross margin and converts 15% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.87x.
ROE of 24% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $8.9M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.0, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.4% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 72% of profits supports about 20.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has missed earnings estimates by 16.5% on average.
own: Insiders own 6.9%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 14%.
